win_claim.quote: The approach has been compared with other neural network learning algorithms specifically designed for dealing with imbalanced datasets, and the results obtained show the competitiveness of the proposal.

uncertain: Metric: paper reports only accuracy CG and minimum sensitivity MS_G; MS is not in the schema priority list, so accuracy CG was chosen; MS_G rows for DSRBF vs SmoteOS are in notes (Table 6, p.10).

SMOTE baseline: SmoteOS (from CSNN [15]) is plain SMOTE preprocessing but with an MLP classifier, while DSRBF uses RBFNN; SSRBF (Table 4, p.8) is SMOTE with the same RBFNN but uses the authors' iterative per-class doubling scheme, so it was not recorded as plain SMOTE.
Balance DSRBF CG printed 93.86 in Table 6 (p.10) but 93.85 in Table 4 (p.8); Glass DSRBF MS SD 22.00 in Table 6 vs 21.99 in Table 4. Copied Table 6 values.
Table 2 (p.6) labels its example the 'zoo' dataset but the initial class counts (70, 76, 17, 13, 9, 29) match Glass in Table 3 (p.8).
Saureus4 source_repo/how_obtained: data taken from refs [57,58] (not UCI); classed as original with 'other' repo (p.9).
Abstract says 13 benchmark datasets plus one microbial growth problem; Sec. 4.1 and conclusions say 12 UCI + 1 (Saureus4) = 13 total; Table 3 lists 13 (pp.1, 7, 12).
n_minority/n_majority filled only for binary datasets from NPPC; left null for multi-class (p.8).
notes: Proposed = DSRBF (dynamic SMOTE radial basis function); SSRBF (static SMOTE) is the authors' second proposed variant and appears with MRBF in Table 4 (p.8) as justification. best_other taken from Table 6 baselines OS, TMNN, SE, HE only (SmoteOS excluded).
